profile.name: Suhaas Srungavarapu
profile.role: I build AI agents where the problem lives, side by side with the people who have it. Then I ship.
profile.status: Incoming AI Builder at Salesforce · New York, Jan 2027
profile.manifesto: I spent two years helping keep a *credit-card platform* online for *20 million people* in 30+ countries. Now I build *AI agents* and ship them *fast.*
profile.about:
I like building things that have a person on the other end.

My first job was on HSBC's credit-card platform in Pune, where reliability was the whole job. It taught me to care about the unglamorous parts: uptime, incident response and getting the details right.

I moved to California for my master's at Santa Clara and found hackathons. A weekend, a team and something that has to work on stage is still my favorite way to learn a new tool. Seven wins later, I haven't stopped.

The same pull took me to the Miller Center, where I designed a learning app for schools in India.

Away from the keyboard I mentor early-career engineers, read, and cook. When I can get outside I'm hiking, exploring somewhere new or playing sports.

I ask why before I build, and I'd rather tell you exactly what I did than oversell it.
profile.contactLine: The fastest way to reach me is email or LinkedIn. My code is on GitHub.

experience.note: Joining through Futureforce, Salesforce's emerging-talent program.

bullets: Part of the team rebuilding a legacy quality-management system for medical-device operations as a modern web app, from scratch.
Mostly backend, working across the full stack: async FastAPI services on PostgreSQL behind a React and TypeScript front end.
Work on the regulated-workflow core: multi-stage, role-based approval routing, 21 CFR Part 11-style e-signatures, segregation of duties and a field-level audit trail.
The codebase is tested at three levels (pytest, Vitest, Playwright) and ships through Jenkins, Docker, Helm and Terraform.
Own the normalization stage of an AI pipeline that turns customer Excel bid sheets, each laid out differently, into one standard workbook for a product-matching agent built by teammates.

Designed it deterministic-first: rules extract what they can and an LLM handles only the ambiguous fields. In offline planning runs on two representative bid formats, that cut planned LLM calls by roughly 50 to 62%.
Ported the normalizer from Node.js to Python so it runs in the same pipeline as the matcher. 19 of 19 offline acceptance tests pass.
Added coverage accounting and source-cell evidence so skipped rows get caught and uncertain results go to a human reviewer.

experience.place: Santa Clara University · placed with Ignis Careers, Hyderabad
bullets: Designed an offline-first, Android-first self-learning app for a social enterprise that teaches English and life skills to about 364K students across 1,542 schools.

Ran the cost and accuracy analysis that settled the speech stack: on-device Whisper-base came out about 50× cheaper than cloud APIs and more accurate on Indian-accented English (13.6% word error rate against 20.9% and 30.0%).
Delivered 7 design documents (49 pages) and 4 clickable prototypes covering about 60 screens. The engagement covered design and architecture; the engineering build was out of scope.
Came back in October 2026 as an AI Mentor at the Miller Center's AI Build Studio, helping social-enterprise founders scope and debug AI prototypes.
Backend engineer on the global credit-card platform: 20M+ users, 30+ countries, 99.98% uptime.
Helped lead India's first mobile card-activation feature, which reached 250K activations in Q1.
Automated 90% of a manual data-conversion process, saving 15+ engineer-hours per release.
Resolved critical incidents 40% faster than the SLA.
